app.title: WinStart
updates.subtitle: What's new in WinStart
updates.installing: Starting the installer — the app will restart by itself.
changelog.1.1.5.1: System file check, component store repair and disk check now show right on the card whether any errors were found.
changelog.1.1.5.2: The Home report and the journal archive save again: the file name no longer causes an error.
changelog.1.1.5.3: Messages from system checks in the journal are no longer shown as garbled characters.
changelog.1.1.4.1: Search across the whole app: the box above the menu (or Ctrl+F) finds functions, programs, sections and answer-file settings.
changelog.1.1.4.2: New Programs section: browsers, messengers, archivers and other popular programs install with one click. The same list can be added to the answer file so the programs install together with Windows.
changelog.1.1.4.3: New Startup section: shows everything that starts with Windows — programs, tasks and services — and lets you turn off what you don't need. Microsoft entries are hidden by default.
changelog.1.1.4.4: Answer file: check a Windows image (ISO or USB stick) — whether language, edition and bitness match; write the file to a USB stick with one click; preview the finished file; table of contents and search inside the form.
changelog.1.1.4.5: The Updates section now checks for a new version by itself and installs it with one click: the app updates and reopens.
changelog.1.1.4.6: A restore point is created with one click in Settings, and the app offers to create one before irreversible actions.
changelog.1.1.4.7: Optimization gained a system file check, component store repair and a disk check.
changelog.1.1.4.8: The Home page can save a report about your computer to a text file.
changelog.1.1.4.9: The Journal together with its backups can be exported to a single archive.
changelog.1.1.3.1: The Answer file section now mirrors the schneegans.de generator completely: every setting, in the same order and with the same explanations. The resulting file is exactly what the website produces.
changelog.1.1.3.2: The computer name and account are no longer pre-filled: Windows picks a random computer name, and the default account is called User.
changelog.1.1.3.3: All progress messages, journal entries and errors are now shown in the selected language.
changelog.1.1.3.4: Fixed a bug in built-in app removal where the Removing banner appeared several times.
changelog.1.1.3.5: The About block was removed from Settings; the version and build date are still shown on Home.
changelog.1.1.2.1: The left menu now looks like glass: the highlight flows smoothly to the section you pick, and its icon lights up in the brand color.
changelog.1.1.2.2: Menu items softly light up when you point at them and gently press in when you click.
changelog.1.1.2.3: The profile card now appears and disappears smoothly, and your PC details show up one by one. Yes / No questions open the same way.
changelog.1.1.2.4: Nothing extra to install anymore: everything WinStart needs to run is built in, so it works even on a freshly installed Windows. Because of this, the installer is larger.
changelog.1.1.1.1: New Answer file section: prepares a file for your Windows install USB stick. With it, Windows installs itself — with your name, language, keyboard layouts and without unwanted apps.
changelog.1.1.1.2: Every answer file setting can be changed and is remembered. The Reset button puts everything back.
changelog.1.1.1.3: Uninstalling WinStart now removes its items from the right-click menu and the programs it downloaded (Unlocker, Everything). No more broken menu items left behind.
changelog.1.1.1.4: Unlocker and Everything now live in their own folder and are kept when you reinstall WinStart.
changelog.1.1.1.5: The version and release date on Home are always visible; the window is slightly larger.
changelog.1.1.1.6: Undoing from the Journal is now complete: files come back too, and Explorer restarts when needed.
changelog.1.1.1.7: What's new and all Home labels are translated into both languages; word endings fixed (for example, “1 day”, “2 days”).
changelog.1.1.1.8: Updated the Windows Defender removal tool: it starts without an extra window and the removal runs all the way through.
changelog.1.1.1: Your profile now sits in the bottom-left corner: your Windows name and account rights. Click it to see your PC specs.
changelog.1.1.2: Home now shows all your drives, graphics card, screen resolution and how long the PC has been running.
changelog.1.1.3: Tick several functions and apply them with a single button. Functions that are already on get turned off.
changelog.1.1.4: Smooth transitions between sections and when opening the profile.
changelog.1.1.6: A dedicated installer: pick the theme and language, and reinstall or remove the app if it is already installed.
changelog.1.1.7: One brand color for both the light and dark themes.
changelog.1.1.8: Fixed Visual C++ installation, Defender removal and switching colored folder icons.
changelog.1.0.2: Sections: Interface, Context menu, Cleanup, Optimization, Software, Components, Miscellaneous.
changelog.1.0.3: Every change can be reverted, and your action history is kept in the journal.
changelog.1.0.4: Light and dark themes, Russian and English.

ua.subtitle: Every setting of the schneegans.de generator, in the same order. Put the resulting autounattend.xml in the root of your install USB drive and Windows installs without questions.
ua.reset.confirm: All settings will return to the original set. Continue?
ua.lang.unattended: Install Windows using these language settings
ua.lang.unattended.desc: Windows features like Settings and File Explorer will appear in this language. It must match the language of your Windows 10/11 image.
ua.lang.locale1.desc: The first language also determines the initial regional format, which defines how numbers, dates, times and currency are formatted. You can change it later.
ua.lang.second: Specify a second language and keyboard layout
ua.lang.third: Specify a third language and keyboard layout
ua.lang.geo: Home location and device setup region
ua.lang.interactive: Select language settings interactively during Windows Setup
ua.pe.interactive: Run the Windows PE stage interactively
ua.pe.interactive.desc: Windows Setup will ask you how to partition your disk and where to install Windows. Choose this when your disk already has partitions that you want to keep.
ua.pe.generate: Generate a .cmd script to handle the Windows PE stage
ua.pe.script: Provide your own .cmd script for the Windows PE stage
ua.pe.script.desc: Your script has to partition and format the disk, make it bootable and copy a Windows image to it. Note that PowerShell is usually not available in Windows PE.
ua.pe.scriptValue: CMD script for the Windows PE stage
ua.pe.dot3.desc: This removes all existing short file names such as PROGRA~1 and disables the creation of new ones.
ua.pe.defender.desc: Windows Defender services will be disabled during the Windows PE stage and thus prevented from ever running.
ua.pe.pauseFormat: Pause before disk is partitioned and formatted
ua.pe.pauseReboot: Pause before Windows Setup reboots at the end of the Windows PE stage
ua.pe.compact: Apply Windows image in compact mode
ua.pe.skipIntegrity: Skip integrity check when applying image
ua.pe.skipIntegrity.desc: This omits the parameters /CheckIntegrity /Verify, which might speed up the imaging operation.
ua.edition.interactive: Enter a product key interactively during Windows Setup
ua.edition.generic: Use a generic product key to install this edition of Windows
ua.edition.generic.desc: Such a key can be used to install Windows, but will not activate it. You can change the product key later.
ua.edition.firmware: Use product key stored in BIOS/UEFI firmware
ua.edition.firmware.desc: Choose this if your computer came pre-installed with Windows and you want to reuse that license.
ua.image.name: Select image with this name
ua.image.name.desc: Run dism.exe /Get-WimInfo /WimFile:"…\install.wim" or Get-WindowsImage -ImagePath "…\install.wim" in PowerShell to learn the name and index of an image inside a .wim file.
ua.image.interactive: Select image interactively during Windows Setup
ua.image.interactive.desc: This shows a list of available images, and you select the image to install by typing in its index.
ua.part.unattended: Let Windows Setup wipe, partition and format your hard drive using these settings
ua.part.custom: Use a custom diskpart script to configure your disk(s)
ua.part.custom.desc: Drive letter assignments in the script (e.g. ASSIGN LETTER=W) solely affect the Windows PE stage of Windows Setup. The new installation will always assign the C: drive letter to the Windows partition.
ua.part.interactive: Run diskpart interactively during Windows Setup
ua.part.interactive.desc: You will have to enter the commands to partition and format your disks. There is no graphical user interface.
ua.target.criteria: Select the target disk based on these criteria
ua.target.criteria.desc: Specify criteria that distinguish the intended target disk from other disks in your computer, such as secondary hard disks or USB flash drives. A generated script will test all available physical disks. If exactly one disk matches all criteria, it will be used as the target disk (and thus be wiped and formatted automatically). Otherwise, Windows Setup will halt to avoid data loss.
ua.target.noPartitions: The target disk must not contain any existing partitions
ua.target.interface: The target disk must be connected to a SATA, SCSI, SAS or NVMe controller
ua.target.media: The target disk must report its media type as Fixed hard disk to the operating system
ua.target.capacity: The target disk must have this capacity
ua.target.index: The target disk must have this index number
ua.target.index.desc: Zero-based. There is no guarantee that disk 0 refers to the primary hard drive – it may very well refer to a USB flash drive instead. You should generally not rely on this criterion alone.
ua.target.script: Provide your own .vbs script for target disk detection
ua.target.script.desc: Your script has to return the index number of the target disk via WScript.Echo. In case of an error, call WScript.Quit 1 – Windows Setup will then halt to avoid data loss.
ua.target.scriptValue: VBS script for target disk detection
ua.target.interactive: Type in the index number interactively during Windows Setup
ua.layout.auto.desc: This detects the firmware type (BIOS or UEFI) and selects the partition layout (MBR or GPT) accordingly.
ua.layout.gpt.desc: The GPT partition layout must be used for UEFI systems.
ua.layout.mbr.desc: The MBR-based partition layout must be used for legacy BIOS systems.
ua.system.desc: This partition is used to boot your computer. On GPT drives, this is known as the EFI System Partition (ESP).
ua.g.re: Choose how to install Windows RE
ua.re.partition.desc: Creates a separate partition of the given size and installs Windows RE to it.
ua.re.none.desc: Windows RE will not be available, and no recovery partition will be created.
ua.assert.skip: Make no assertions about the target disk
ua.assert.generated: Make these assertions about the target disk
ua.assert.capacity: Assert that the target disk has a capacity within these limits
ua.assert.noPartitions: Assert that there are no partitions on the target disk
ua.assert.interface: Assert that the target disk is connected to a SATA, SCSI, SAS or NVMe controller
ua.assert.media: Assert that the target disk reports its media type as Fixed hard disk to the operating system
ua.assert.script: Provide your own .vbs script for disk verification
ua.paging.auto: Let Windows manage paging file size
ua.activation.key.desc: If you have already entered a product key above, you do not need to repeat that key here.
ua.s.arch.desc: When you select multiple processor architectures, a single autounattend.xml file is created that is applicable to all of them.
ua.setup.bypass: Bypass Windows 11 requirements check (TPM, Secure Boot, etc.)
ua.setup.bypass.desc: Applies when the Windows PE stage is run interactively.
ua.setup.network: Allow Windows 11 to be installed without internet connection
ua.setup.network.desc: Only check this option if your computer really does not have internet access. You will still have to click the I don't have internet button during Windows Setup in that case. If you just want to create local accounts in Windows 11, you do not need this option – simply use the User accounts section.
ua.setup.configSet: Use a distribution share / configuration set ($OEM$ folder)
ua.setup.configSet.desc: This makes Windows Setup look for a folder named $OEM$ in the root of the drive where your autounattend.xml file is located and copy its contents to the target partition.
ua.setup.hidePs: Hide any PowerShell windows during Windows Setup
ua.setup.hidePs.desc: By default, PowerShell scripts have a visible window. This makes debugging easier and lets you use interactive prompts, but the window could be closed inadvertently, which would kill the script. Do not hide the windows if you plan to use interactive prompts (like Read-Host) – without a visible window you could not answer them, and Windows Setup could not continue.
ua.setup.keepFiles.desc: By default, the files C:\Windows\Panther\unattend.xml, C:\Windows\Panther\unattend-original.xml and C:\Windows\Setup\Scripts\Wifi.xml, which may contain sensitive data, are deleted once Windows Setup has finished. With this option they are kept.
ua.setup.narrator: Automatically start Narrator during Windows Setup and after logon
ua.setup.narrator.desc: Narrator is a built-in screen reader that speaks out loud what is on your screen.
ua.computer.random: Let Windows generate a random computer name like DESKTOP-ZFAH8Z2
ua.computer.name: Computer name
ua.computer.script: Provide a Windows PowerShell script to set the computer name dynamically
ua.computer.script.desc: Your script will be evaluated during Windows Setup. It must return a single string, which must be a valid computer name. Use a script such as return Read-Host -Prompt 'Enter computer name'; to create an interactive prompt.
ua.tz.implicit: Let Windows determine your time zone based on language and region settings
ua.tz.explicit.desc: This is useful when your country or region spans multiple time zones, like Russia, Australia or the United States.
ua.acc.unattended: Let Windows Setup create the following local accounts
ua.acc.name: Account name
ua.acc.display.desc: Leave Display name empty unless you want it to be different from Account name.
ua.g.firstLogon.desc: Several settings are only applied when an administrator logs on for the first time. You should therefore let Windows log you on to an administrator account once – this does not affect subsequent logons.
ua.logon.own: Logon to the first administrator account created above
ua.logon.builtin: Activate the built-in account Administrator, logon to this account and set its password
ua.logon.none.desc: The installation ends with the sign-in screen being shown. Not recommended.
ua.acc.obscure: Obscure all account passwords in your autounattend.xml file with Base64
ua.acc.microsoft: Add a Microsoft ("online") user account interactively during Windows Setup
ua.acc.local: Add a local ("offline") user account interactively during Windows Setup
ua.pw.unlimited.desc: This is in accordance with NIST guidelines that no longer recommend password expiration.
ua.pw.custom.desc: These settings only apply to local accounts. Also, the password of the built-in account Administrator never expires.
ua.lock.default.desc: By default, Windows locks out an account after 10 failed logon attempts (threshold) within 10 minutes (window). After 10 minutes (duration), the account is unlocked automatically.
ua.lock.disable.desc: Disabling Account Lockout might leave your computer vulnerable to brute-force attacks.
ua.files.hidden.desc: This hides any file that has the Hidden attribute set.
ua.files.hiddenSystem.desc: This only hides files that have both the Hidden and the System attribute set.
ua.files.none.desc: This setting is recommended for advanced users.
ua.explorer.ext.desc: By default, File Explorer hides extensions for known file types.
ua.explorer.classic: Use classic context (right-click) menu in Windows 11
ua.explorer.infotip: Hide pop-up description for folder and desktop items
ua.explorer.thisPc: Open File Explorer to This PC instead of Quick access
ua.explorer.endTask: Show End task command in the taskbar
ua.search.title: Search box in the taskbar
ua.search.label: Icon and label
ua.tbicons.title: Icons in the taskbar
ua.tbicons.custom: Configure icons using an XML file
ua.tbicons.custom.desc: See Microsoft's Taskbar layout documentation for more examples.
ua.tb.widgets.desc: This hides the news and weather widget in the lower-left corner in Windows 11.
ua.tb.taskview: Hide the Task view button from the taskbar
ua.tb.tray.desc: On Windows 10, this simply sets the EnableAutoTray registry value. On Windows 11, this creates a scheduled task that runs periodically in the background and sets all tray icons visible.
ua.tb.bing: Do not show Bing results when searching in the Start menu or the search box
ua.tiles.default.desc: If you select apps in the Remove bloatware section below, Windows 10 automatically removes their tiles from the Start menu.
ua.tiles.custom: Configure tiles using an XML file
ua.tiles.custom.desc: Created by PowerShell's Export-StartLayout cmdlet on another Windows 10 computer.
ua.pins.default.desc: Avoid this setting if you select apps in the Remove bloatware section below, as Windows 11 deceptively retains their pins in the Start menu.
ua.pins.custom: Configure pins using a JSON file
ua.pins.custom.desc: Created by PowerShell's Export-StartLayout cmdlet on another Windows 11 computer.
ua.sys.update.desc: This creates a scheduled task (named PauseWindowsUpdate) that pauses updates for one week again and again. To run Windows Update once, click Resume updates in Settings. To enable Windows Update permanently, disable or delete that task.
ua.sys.uac.desc: Not recommended with a Microsoft ("online") user account, as Windows Hello PIN dialogs might appear minimized or hidden. Disable UAC only for testing environments or when you intend to use separate administrator and user accounts.
ua.sys.sac.desc: This turns Smart App Control off in Windows 11. Note that you will not be able to turn it back on.
ua.sys.smartscreen: Disable SmartScreen in Windows and Edge
ua.sys.restore.desc: Windows will not create restore points for drive C: and thus use less disk space.
ua.sys.longPaths.desc: This sets the LongPathsEnabled registry value, which enables several programs (including PowerShell, 7-Zip and TreeSize) to use long paths with up to 32,767 characters without the \\?\ prefix.
ua.sys.acl.desc: This removes write permissions on C:\ for the Authenticated Users group. In particular, this prevents unprivileged users from creating bogus folders such as C:\Windows.
ua.sys.junctions.desc: This deletes several hidden junction points, such as C:\Documents and Settings or C:\Users\Default\My Documents. These were intended to improve compatibility with older software, but can be quite confusing.
ua.sys.ps: Allow execution of PowerShell script files
ua.sys.ps.desc: This runs the command Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy 'RemoteSigned', which allows the execution of unsigned .ps1 files.
ua.sys.lastAccess: Do not update Last Access Time stamp
ua.sys.lastAccess.desc: This runs the command fsutil.exe behavior set disableLastAccess 1, which can improve file system performance.
ua.sys.noReboot: Prevent Windows Update from rebooting your computer
ua.sys.noReboot.desc: This creates a scheduled task that periodically moves your active hours, tricking Windows into thinking your device is in use all the time.
ua.sys.sounds.desc: This changes the sound scheme from Windows Default to No sounds for all users.
ua.sys.suggestions: Disable app suggestions / Content Delivery Manager
ua.sys.suggestions.desc: This sets several registry values that prevent the silent download and installation of suggested apps. As a side effect this also disables the Manage devices button in the Mobile devices section in Settings. If this bothers you, change the value of DisableWindowsConsumerFeatures to 0.
ua.sys.encryption.desc: Windows 11 would otherwise enable BitLocker encryption automatically.
ua.sys.edgeFre.desc: This skips the annoying dialogs when Edge is run for the first time.
ua.sys.edgeBoost: Disable Edge Startup Boost and Background mode
ua.sys.edgeBoost.desc: This stops Edge from running in the background all the time.
ua.sys.edgeUninstall.desc: This modifies the C:\Windows\System32\IntegratedServicesRegionPolicySet.json file such that Edge can be uninstalled even outside the European Economic Area. This setting tends to cause problems with Windows Update. Use at your own risk!
ua.sys.pointer: Disable the Enhance Pointer Precision mouse setting
ua.sys.pointer.desc: This may be useful for players of first-person shooters.
ua.sys.restartSignOn: Disable automatic sign-on of last user after a restart
ua.sys.restartSignOn.desc: By default, Windows automatically signs on the last user after a restart and then locks their session. This offers very little benefit compared to signing on manually and often leads to a confusing warning.
ua.sys.wpbt: Disable Windows Platform Binary Table (WPBT) execution
ua.sys.deviceApps: Prevent download and installation of applications associated with certain hardware devices
ua.sys.deviceApps.desc: LG monitors, for example, have come under scrutiny for automatically installing unwanted software.
ua.sys.audit.desc: Each time a new process is created, Windows writes an event to the Security log. This is a powerful tool for troubleshooting.
ua.sys.auditCmd: Include command line in log events
ua.effects.default: Use default settings chosen by Windows
ua.fx.ControlAnimations: Animate controls and elements inside windows
ua.fx.AnimateMinMax: Animate windows when minimizing and maximizing
ua.fx.MenuAnimation: Fade or slide menus into view
ua.fx.TooltipAnimation: Fade or slide ToolTips into view
ua.fx.SelectionFade: Fade out menu items after clicking
ua.fx.ListviewShadow: Use drop shadows for icon labels on the desktop
ua.folders.default: Show default folders on Start next to the Power button
ua.folders.custom.desc: This setting has no effect on Windows 10. On Windows 11, the folders appear on the Start menu next to the Power button.
ua.core.keep: Keep core isolation enabled if supported
ua.core.keep.desc: To enable virtualization-based security and make use of Windows virtualization features including Hyper-V, WSL2, Docker and Windows Sandbox.
ua.core.disable.desc: To prioritize performance (especially in games) and to allow for third-party virtualization software such as VMware Workstation or VirtualBox.
ua.s.vmguest.desc: Guest additions are installed when Windows runs inside a virtual machine.
ua.vm.virtio: Install VirtIO drivers, VirtIO Guest Tools and QEMU Guest Agent
ua.vm.parallels: Install Parallels Tools for Parallels Desktop
ua.wifi.interactive: Configure Wi‑Fi interactively during Windows Setup
ua.wifi.skip.desc: Choose this if you have a wired connection to the internet.
ua.wifi.driver.desc: If Windows does not support your Wi‑Fi adapter out-of-the-box, you need to add the appropriate driver files to the $WinPEDriver$ folder on your installation medium.
ua.wifi.xml: Configure Wi‑Fi using an XML file
ua.wifi.xml.desc: Created by netsh.exe wlan export profile key=clear on another computer.
ua.express.disable.desc: Windows will not send diagnostic data, personalized input or your location history to Microsoft. Choose this if you value privacy.
ua.express.enable.desc: Windows will send data to Microsoft to provide location-based services, improve language recognition, and show personalized ads.
ua.express.interactive: Choose settings interactively during Windows Setup
ua.express.interactive.desc: This lets you enable some settings while disabling others.
ua.lk.default: Use default lock key states and behaviors
ua.lk.custom: Configure the initial state and behavior of lock keys
ua.lk.custom.desc: This affects all users and also the login screen.
ua.sticky.custom.desc: This affects all users and also the login screen.
ua.sticky.HotKeyActive: Press the Shift key 5 times to turn Sticky keys on or off
ua.sticky.HotKeySound: Play a siren sound when Sticky keys are turned on or off by using the Shift key
ua.sticky.Indicator: Show the Sticky keys icon on the taskbar
ua.sticky.AudibleFeedback: Play a sound when shortcut keys are pressed and released
ua.sticky.TriState: Lock shortcut keys when pressed twice in a row
ua.sticky.TwoKeysOff: Turn off Sticky keys when two keys are pressed at the same time
ua.colors.system: Color theme for taskbar and Start menu
ua.colors.onStart: Show accent color on Start menu and taskbar
ua.colors.onBorders: Show accent color on title bars and window borders
ua.wp.script: Provide a Windows PowerShell script to load a desktop wallpaper image
ua.wp.script.desc: Your script will be evaluated during Windows Setup, after your computer has connected to a network. The script must return a byte[] value, which must contain the raw image data.
ua.ls.script: Provide a Windows PowerShell script to load the lock screen image
ua.ls.script.desc: This script works just as the Desktop wallpaper script above.
ua.ls.scriptValue: PowerShell script for lock screen image
ua.s.bloat.desc: Note that it might be difficult to reinstall removed apps, particularly the Microsoft Store app.
ua.g.scriptsSystem.desc: These scripts run in the system context, before user accounts are created.
ua.g.scriptsDefaultUser.desc: Use these scripts to modify the default user's registry hive. The generated code automatically mounts the C:\Users\Default\NTUSER.DAT hive file, runs your scripts and unmounts the hive again. DefaultUser scripts run after System scripts, but still before user accounts are created. Hence, they affect all user accounts, including the built-in account Administrator.
ua.g.scriptsFirstLogon.desc: These scripts run when the first user logs on after Windows has been installed. The first user to log on is typically an administrator; in this case the scripts run with elevated privileges.
ua.g.scriptsUserOnce.desc: These scripts run whenever a user logs on for the first time.
ua.scripts.restartExplorer: Restart File Explorer after scripts have run
ua.scripts.restartExplorer.desc: This restarts the explorer.exe process that is responsible for displaying Start menu, taskbar and Desktop. If your scripts make changes to any of these elements, check this box so that they take effect immediately.
ua.s.components.desc: For advanced users: pick a component and a setup pass and paste the markup that goes inside its component element. Pairs that already have markup are marked with a dot.

ua.check.title: Image and USB stick
ua.check.desc: Check that the answer file matches your Windows image: language, edition and bitness must agree. Point to an ISO file, install.wim or a USB stick with the installer.
ua.check.placeholder: Path to an ISO, install.wim or installer folder
ua.check.reading: Reading image {0}… For an ISO this takes 10–30 seconds.
ua.check.noWim: No install.wim or install.esd inside — this is not a Windows installation image.
ua.check.noMount: Could not open the ISO file.
ua.check.langAsk: The language is chosen during setup — nothing to check.
ua.check.langSome: Language {0} is not in every edition of the image (present in: {1}).
ua.check.langMissing: The image has no {0} language (available: {1}). Setup will stop with an error — choose another language or image.
ua.check.editionMissing: The image has no "{0}" edition. Available: {1}.
ua.check.nameDiffers: Setup will look for an image named "{0}", but in this image it is called "{1}". Choose "Select the image with this name" and enter "{1}", or use index {2}.
ua.check.indexMissing: There is no image with index {0} — the file has only {1}.
ua.check.editionAsk: The edition is chosen during setup — nothing to check.
ua.check.archMismatch: The image is for {0}, but the answer file targets {1}. Tick the right one under "Processor architecture".
ua.check.win10: This is a Windows 10 image. Most settings apply, but they were tested on Windows 11.
